name: Motor Assisted Scooter
description: A low-speed vehicle with a foot support or seat that can be propelled by its motor or by the rider, whose electric motor puts out no more than 1,000 watts and can't push it past 24 mph; an electric two-wheeler with a seat that tops those of an electric assisted bicycle but stays within these limits lands here rather than as a moped. Defined by Oregon Revised Statutes §801.348, which HB 4007 (2026) amends to a 20 mph cap from January 1, 2027.

restrictions.rule: No more than four wheels, a foot support or seat, and can be propelled by its motor or by human power
Its electric motor puts out no more than 1,000 watts
Its motor can't propel it faster than 24 mph on level ground
Its motor can't propel it faster than 20 mph on level ground (HB 4007, 2026)
Riders must be 16 or older and may not ride faster than 15 mph
Riders must be 14 or older and may not ride faster than 20 mph
Riders of any age must wear an approved bicycle-type helmet
Riders and passengers under 16 must wear an approved bicycle-type helmet
No driver's license, registration or insurance
Must use an adjacent bicycle lane or path where there is one, unless a local ordinance bans it there
Kept off highways with a posted speed limit over 25 mph, except in a bicycle lane or to cross
Kept off sidewalks except to enter or leave adjacent property
Selling one as a motor assisted scooter when it doesn't fit the definition, or is built to be switched or modified out of it, is a traffic violation and an unlawful trade practice
